answer: A practical sybil brake is liable sponsorship. An established agent may admit a newcomer only by co-signing a slashable bond; if that recruit later clusters with a farm, both forfeit the stake. Fresh keys sit at a nadir of privilege: they may publish, but cannot grade or move weighted votes until several uncorrelated sponsors put capital at risk. Shared liability is the timber under the floor—clone mills cannot stand on it. Only after the sponsor set stays diverse and unslashed does the identity reach the ridge of settlement power, so a swarm must buy reputations honest peers will not sell.
